newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end mixed after brisk session.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end mixed after brisk session.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks finished mixed in heavy trading * Gains in consumer products, conglomerates offset by weak golds, banks * 14 sub-groups evenly split * 83 million shrs traded worth C$1 bln
Toronto stocks ended mixed on Friday, with scattered gains offset by weak gold prices and profit-taking among the banks.
The TSE 300 Composite Index eased 3.57 points to close at 5301.05 in heavy turnover of 83 million shares valued at C$1.09 billion.
But advancing stocks still outnumbered declines 472 to 404 with 308 issues unchanged.
"There is still some underlying strength in the market, but once in a while people have to take profits," said Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading for ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
Financial services dropped 19 points as profit-takers hit bank stocks for a second straight day.
Bank shares have soared recently after some analysts raised their price targets for the so-called Big Six banks.

The precious metals group extended Thursday's losses, falling 47 points today. COMEX gold futures sank further as investors continue to react negatively to the IMF's plan to sell some gold reserves to help fund Third World debt relief.
"The IMF did not amuse the big gold miners of the world and so we're seeing weakness in that sector," Ketchen said.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Pegasus Gold Inc. avoided the weak trend in golds, jumping 0.55 to 14.20 on news that its proposed merger with Dayton Mining Corp. will not proceed.
Dayton Mining fell 0.55 to 9.20 on 1.6 million shares.
* Among the banks, Royal Bank of Canada dropped 0.35 to 38.80, while Toronto-Dominion Bank fell 0.25 to 27.40.
* Seagram Co Ltd powered a 45-point gain in consumer products. The spirits and entertainment giant closed up 0.60 at 52 on 180,000 shares.
* Clearnet Communications class A rose 1.75 to 22.45 after announcing a new wireless business communications network.
